body:
## Affected Packages

Don't know

## Problem

When using npm, running `changeset version` does not update the version in the lock file. 

This does not appear to have any ill effect and may be purely cosmetic

## Proposed solution

Running `npm install` ensures that the version is updated

comments.body: I think this is purely cosmetic as you said, but I'm curious if any package maintainers here have any input on this.

It (`package-lock.json` update) would be a nice additional flag to set... In a manual flow, it comes up to just running `npm install` additionally I guess. I actually use the corresponding GitHub action which creates a PR with the version increment, maybe there's a possibility to tweak it somehow now?
But `npm install` also tries to update dependencies.

I am new to changesets, and this may be a dumb question.

Is there a reason not to use `npm version`? It automatically updates package.json and the lock file.

I would find it useful to update the lockfiles as part of the versioning process. We use git hooks to run testing on commit, and part of that is re-running npm i and build.
Currently, the lockfiles appear as extra files when this runs after a release, so I need to do a second commit just for syncing the package-lock file to the correct version.

And further to what @almahdi404 said, npm install doesn't update dependencies if a lockfile already exists, you might be thinking of npm update

title: Version not updated in package-lock.json
